chief_complaint: alternating diarrhea and constipation with abdominal cramping for 6 months
hpi_details: A 29-year-old male presents to the clinic with alternating diarrhea and constipation with abdominal cramping for 6 months. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: He thinks his erratic meal schedule and heavy stress at work have thrown his digestive system completely off track.
concerns: He is worried that an urgent bathroom rush during his commute or client meetings will cause public embarrassment and cost him his job.
expectations: He hopes to receive medication to calm his painful stomach spasms and advice on how to normalize his bowel movements.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes recommending dietary modifications (low-FODMAP diet) and stress reduction, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

Key HPI features: A 29-year-old male presents to the clinic with alternating diarrhea and constipation with abdominal cramping for 6 months. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Irritable Bowel Syndrome.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Inflammatory bowel disease without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: rectal bleeding or blood in the stool, unintentional weight loss, or nocturnal symptoms that wake the patient from sleep.
management_principles: Recommend dietary modifications (Low-FODMAP diet), stress reduction
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 29-year-old male presents with a 6-month history of alternating diarrhoea and constipation with abdominal cramping, no red-flag features on screening.
reference_soap.objective: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Irritable Bowel Syndrome.
reference_soap.assessment: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), mixed bowel habit subtype. DDx: inflammatory bowel disease, coeliac disease, colorectal cancer.
reference_soap.plan: Recommend dietary modifications (Low-FODMAP diet), stress reduction. Consult specialist if symptoms worsen. Counsel patient.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Irritable Bowel Syndrome
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Irritable Bowel Syndrome
Implement evidence-based management plan: Recommend dietary modifications (Low-FODMAP diet), stress reduction

teaching.one_liner: A functional gut disorder where stress and certain foods trigger cramping and alternating bowel habits, without any structural disease on testing.
red_flags: Rectal bleeding or blood in the stool — atypical for IBS and warrants investigation for IBD or malignancy
Unintentional weight loss — raises concern for organic pathology rather than a functional disorder
Nocturnal symptoms that wake the patient from sleep — not typical of IBS and suggest an organic cause

must_ask.say: Do you swing between diarrhoea and constipation, or is it just one or the other?
Does the cramping ease once you've had a bowel movement?
Do your symptoms flare up more when you're stressed?
Are there any foods that seem to set it off?
Have you ever noticed blood in your stool?
Have you lost any weight without trying to?

history.answer: I have been dealing with alternating diarrhea and constipation, along with stomach cramps, for about six months now.
When I am constipated, I only go once every three or four days with hard lumps and straining, but during diarrhea bouts, I go three or four times a day with watery stools.
It started gradually about six months ago, and over the past month or two it has become more noticeable and bothersome.
I often feel like my bowels are not completely empty after going, but I have never needed to push on my stomach or use my fingers.
I have not noticed pencil-thin stools, but the shape keeps swinging between small hard pellets and completely watery stools.
No, I have never seen red blood on the toilet paper or in the bowl, and my stools have never looked black or tarry.
I get cramping pain in my lower stomach with bloating, and having a bowel movement or passing gas usually brings relief.
Yes, they keep taking turns—I will be severely constipated for three or four days, and then I will have loose diarrhea for a couple of days.
I can pass gas without any trouble, and I have not had any nausea or vomiting.
No, my weight has remained completely stable at around seventy-two kilograms.
No, I do not feel sharp cutting or tearing pain around my anus when I pass stool.
I have felt generally tired and fatigued lately, but I have not had cold intolerance, weight gain, or unusually dry skin.
No, my thirst and urination habits have been completely normal.
I do not take opioid painkillers, iron, or calcium supplements, and I have not used any laxatives.
I drink about one liter of water a day, eat regular meals though I often eat takeout, and jog about once a week.
I do not hold in my bowel movements, but work has been very stressful lately, and stress seems to make the cramps worse.
I have never had a colonoscopy or any other bowel scope done before.
Eating greasy takeout, drinking coffee, or having dairy seems to trigger the cramping and loose bowel movements.
No, the cramping or diarrhea has never woken me up from my sleep at night.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, or night sweats at all.
I thought maybe the crazy stress at my job and eating junk food late at night just completely messed up my digestion.
I'm really worried that an urgent bathroom dash in the middle of a client presentation will humiliate me and ruin my career.
I was hoping you could give me something to stop these painful cramps and get my bathroom schedule back to normal.
I do not have any chronic medical illnesses or ongoing health problems.
I have never had surgery and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I am not taking any prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, or dietary supplements.
I do not have any known allergies to medications, foods, or materials.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used tobacco products.
I only drink socially, usually just a beer or two on the weekend with friends.
I work as an office administrator and live alone in an apartment.
Both of my parents are healthy, and there is no family history of colon cancer, polyps, or inflammatory bowel disease.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 120/78 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, body temperature 36.7 degrees Celsius, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Alert, well-appearing young male in no acute distress.
Conjunctivae are pink without pallor; sclerae are clear and anicteric.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, smooth, non-tender, and without palpable nodules.
Abdomen is flat and non-distended, with no scars, rashes, or visible peristalsis.
Normoactive bowel sounds heard in all four quadrants; no arterial bruits.
Tympanitic notes throughout the abdomen, with normal liver span and no shifting dullness.
Abdomen is soft with mild tenderness over the lower abdomen, but no palpable mass, fecal impaction, or rigidity.
No rebound tenderness or peritoneal signs anywhere in the abdomen.
Perianal inspection shows no fissures or external hemorrhoids; digital examination reveals normal sphincter tone, no palpable masses or fecal impaction, and empty rectal vault.
Skin is warm with normal turgor, no abnormal dryness, and no jaundice or rashes.
Deep tendon reflexes are 2+ bilaterally, with normal relaxation phase at both ankles.
